title: Missouri's 3rd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Missouri's 3rd Congressional District will determine who represents this east-central Missouri district — which includes parts of St. Charles County, Jefferson City, and surrounding areas — in the U.S. House of Representatives. First-term Republican incumbent Bob Onder, a physician and attorney elected in 2024, is seeking re-election in a district rated Solid Republican by the Cook Political Report (R+10). The Democratic primary features three contenders — Bethany Mann, Tommy Holstein, and Paul T. Wilson — while the Republican primary pits Onder against challenger John G. Fraser. Independent candidate Theodis Brown Sr. and Libertarian Jim Higgins are also on the ballot. The race takes place against the backdrop of ongoing legal challenges to Missouri's newly redrawn congressional map.

candidates.name: Bob Onder
candidates.summary: Bob Onder is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Missouri's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A physician and attorney, he previously served in the Missouri House of Representatives and the Missouri Senate, where he was Assistant Majority Floor Leader. He serves on the House Judiciary, Transportation and Infrastructure, and Education and the Workforce committees.

candidates.name: Bethany Mann
candidates.summary: Bethany Mann is a progressive Democratic candidate running for Missouri's 3rd Congressional District. She holds a degree in Chemistry and previously worked as an intern at the Environmental Protection Agency; she now works as a technology specialist serving agriculture, energy, and pharmaceutical laboratories. Mann ran for this seat in 2024 and lost to incumbent Bob Onder.

candidates.name: Tommy Holstein
candidates.summary: Tommy Holstein is a Democratic candidate for Missouri's 3rd Congressional District. A Lindenwood University graduate, he founded and runs VideoPunk, a video production agency. He serves as a board member of Destination Imagination and as a fraternity chapter advisor, and is running on a progressive platform focused on Medicare for All, fully funded public education, and AI regulation.

candidates.name: John G. Fraser
candidates.summary: John G. Fraser is a Republican candidate challenging incumbent Bob Onder in the August 2026 primary for Missouri's 3rd Congressional District. He is a certified public accountant (CPA) based in Columbia, Missouri, with training in economics. Fraser emphasizes constitutional governance and fiscal responsibility in his campaign.

forecast.rationale: No published polls exist in the race data (based_on_poll_count=0), so this forecast is driven entirely by district fundamentals. Missouri's 3rd District is rated Solid Republican with a Cook PVI of R+10, providing a strong structural GOP advantage. Incumbent Bob Onder (R) is seeking a second term after winning in 2024; while first-term incumbents can be slightly more vulnerable than entrenched ones, the district's partisan lean is formidable. The Democratic primary field has three contenders (Mann, Holstein, Wilson) but no candidate has demonstrated top-tier fundraising or national support based on available data. The Republican primary challenger (Fraser) is a CPA with no indication of a serious threat to Onder. Minor-party candidates (Libertarian Higgins, Independent Brown) are perennial or long-shot candidates. Ongoing legal challenges to Missouri's redrawn congressional map inject some uncertainty about district lines, but no specific court ruling altering the configuration is reflected in the current race data. With no polling and only fundamentals to rely on, confidence is medium, but the Republican advantage appears overwhelming.
